value.body: A BBA track on how goods are bought, stored and moved — logistics and transport management, warehousing and inventory control, procurement, supply-chain planning, export-import basics, and the ERP and supply-chain software used to run them. Many programmes include an internship at a warehouse, transporter or e-commerce fulfilment centre.

items.label: Regulator
items.note: Alongside the affiliating university; BBA, BCA and BMS were brought under AICTE from 2024-25

items.label: Logistics cost in India
items.note: Estimated at 7.97%; a measure of the sector's size, not of jobs

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 in any stream. Admission is by Class 12 marks, CUET-UG, or a university's own test. Some institutes admit directly to a named BBA (Logistics / Supply Chain) programme; at others you pick the specialisation in the second or third year.

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is close to the ground — warehouses, transport hubs, ports and e-commerce fulfilment centres — and can involve shifts or site postings.
Entry roles include logistics coordinator, warehouse or inventory executive, procurement executive and supply-chain associate.
Spreadsheet and ERP skills (for example SAP) are commonly expected.
Common next steps: an MBA (Operations or Supply Chain), or certifications in supply chain or lean methods.
